text: There was a man of Hawaii. <break time="0.8s" /> Named Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was poor but brave. <break time="0.8s" /> And who could read and write. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a schoolmaster. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a sailor. <break time="0.8s" /> And one day. <break time="0.8s" /> His ship took him to San Francisco. <break time="0.8s" /> A great city on the coast of America. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking up a hill in the city. <break time="0.8s" /> He stopped in front of a small but beautiful house. <break time="0.8s" /> With bright windows. <break time="0.8s" /> At one of the windows. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood an old man. <break time="0.8s" /> Who looked out at Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> With a face full of sadness. <break time="0.8s" /> What a fine house this is thought Keawe. <break time="0.8s" /> If I lived in a house like that I would laugh all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man invited him inside. <break time="0.8s" /> And brought out a round bellied bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> With a long neck. <break time="0.8s" /> Made of glass as white as milk. <break time="0.8s" /> An imp lives in this bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the old man. <break time="0.8s" /> And Keawe saw something move inside it. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a shadow and a fire. <break time="0.8s" /> It was this very bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That had made Napoleon. <break time="0.8s" /> The king of the world. <break time="0.8s" /> But you must sell it. <break time="0.8s" /> For less than you paid. <break time="0.8s" /> And if you die with it. <break time="0.8s" /> You will burn in the fire forever. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man had paid ninety dollars for it. <break time="0.8s" /> And he sold it to Keawe for fifty. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was exactly all the money. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawe had.
